summary: This Wikipedia-derived note is a biographical entry for Maya Pedersen-Bieri, a Swiss-Norwegian skeleton racer who has competed since 1995. It covers her birth, her gold medal in women's skeleton at the 2006 Turin Winter Olympics, her 2010 retirement, and her return to compete for Norway in 2016. It also notes her husband and coach, Snorre Pedersen, and her listing in the IBSF athlete registration system under the name Maya Pedersen.
one_line: Swiss-Norwegian skeleton racer, 2006 Turin Olympic women's skeleton gold medalist, who retired in 2010 and returned to race for Norway.
key_facts: Maya Pedersen-Bieri was born on 27 November 1972 in Spiez.
Maya Pedersen-Bieri is a Swiss-Norwegian skeleton racer who has competed since 1995.
Maya Pedersen-Bieri won the gold medal in the women's skeleton event at the 2006 Winter Olympics in Turin.
Maya Pedersen-Bieri retired from skeleton in 2010.
Maya Pedersen-Bieri returned to compete for Norway in 2016.
Snorre Pedersen is the husband and coach of Maya Pedersen-Bieri.
Maya Pedersen-Bieri returned to the top level of skeleton in 2017, and the note says she became the oldest woman to start a World Cup race.
Maya Pedersen-Bieri is listed in the International Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation athlete registration system as Maya Pedersen.
